subject.title: sessions_spawn from a CLI-harness parent (claude-cli) clamps subagents to gateway bridge tools — children lose exec/read/write

question: How should OpenClaw model CLI-harness native coding capabilities when computing inherited child tool allowlists for `sessions_spawn`?
rationale: The current behavior breaks CLI-harness delegated coding work, but changing inherited allow semantics can either widen or narrow a parent-to-child authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Harness-aware inheritance
options.body: Distinguish CLI bridge-visible tools from native CLI capabilities and persist inherited allowlists only for actual configured restrictions or translated native-capability policy.

options.title: Explicit inheritance switch
options.body: Add a documented subagent inheritance opt-out or mode only if maintainers want operators to choose this compatibility/security tradeoff per setup.

options.title: Keep strict bridge-surface inheritance
options.body: Preserve current non-escalating semantics and document that CLI-backend parents are not suitable delegators for embedded coding children without a different runtime path.

recommendation.title: Harness-aware inheritance
recommendation.body: Distinguish CLI bridge-visible tools from native CLI capabilities and persist inherited allowlists only for actual configured restrictions or translated native-capability policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current area owner signal for sessions_spawn, scoped capability profiles, and the security-sensitive agent runtime policy boundary.
